transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Lakshmi Singh.
President Trump says the U.S. will not attack Iran before next month's midterm elections.
He announced it on social media a short time ago amid low public approval ratings over
the economic fallout from the U.S. war with Iran.
And data have directly tied higher fuel prices and rising inflation to the war.
The White House says Microsoft is being suspended from a program to apply for green cards for
skilled foreign workers.
NPR's Franco Ordonez reports Vice President J.D. Vance accused Microsoft of replacing qualified
U.S. workers with foreign indentured servants.
Vance blasted the tech giant for allegedly abusing the program that's associated with
H-1B visas to provide visas to skilled foreign workers in order to replace American workers
with cheaper foreign labor.
Vance alleged that Microsoft replaced 6,000 American workers with 6,300 foreign workers
on H-1B visas.
If you do the math, for every worker that Microsoft laid off, they replaced that worker
with one and a half foreign indentured servants.
The Trump administration has long targeted the H-1B program.
Vance told Real America's Voice earlier this month that the program was completely broken
and that he'd be OK if it was eliminated.
Franco Ordonez and PR News, the White House.
Hurricane Isaias could make landfall on the northern Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday.
It is the first Atlantic hurricane of 2026.
It has been more than a hundred years since the Atlantic area got its first hurricane
of the season this late.
Forecasters believe Isaias will grow into a category two hurricane before hitting the
coast.
After more than 10 months at sea, the aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln returns to San
Diego today.
Member Station KPBS reporter Andrew Dyer is on the pier waiting on the ship.
He's among the most closely watched and anticipated homecomings in recent memory.
The Lincoln's crew endured shortages of food and other supplies while launching strikes
against Iran.
The ship spent more than eight consecutive months at sea without stopping in port.
Six hours before the ship is due, Ashley de la Fuente is already here waiting.
Her son Christopher is a firefighter on the Lincoln.
When it comes to the hardships during deployment, she says he didn't say much.
Just thought it was rough, you know, this not really much conversation.
I think he was just trying to not scare me so much, put me in my feelings, just kind
of keep me at ease.
So only a little bit of pieces just that it was rough.
The Lincoln is due parasite around noon Pacific time.
For NPR News, I'm Andrew Dyer in San Diego.
From Washington, this is NPR News.
His shipping has become more dangerous in the Strait of Hormuz due to the U.S. war with
Iran.
A U.K.-based maritime security and risk management company says threats to vessels are increasing
the Black Sea due to Russia's war with Ukraine.
The Black Sea is a major commercial shipping route.
Three Turkish-owned vessels were targeted in the past week, killing at least two people.
And Pierre's Hadil al-Shalchi has details.
The Maritime Security Assessment Company, Ambri Analytics, said that the attacks on
the Turkish-owned vessels were "highly likely to be conducted by Russian forces."
The ships were in Romanian and Bulgarian waters.
Two of the vessels sank, and two crew members were killed, according to Romanian authorities.
This has raised concerns of an expansion of the Russian war with Ukraine.
Turkish officials expressed "serious concern" over the attacks, and said Turkish President
Erdogan spoke to Russian President Putin.
Ambri said the incidents in Bulgarian waters mark the first direct strikes against merchant
shipping since the beginning of Russia's invasion of Ukraine.
Hadil al-Shalchi, NPR News.
Ousted Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro is now facing U.S. charges that he conspired
to torture fellow Venezuelans in an attempt to hold onto power.
An indictment was unsealed today showing the Trump administration added the torture charge
to drug trafficking charges against Maduro and his wife Celia Flores.
The couple have been in prison since U.S. forces seized them from their home in the middle
of the night nine months ago.
The couple is pleaded not guilty in the drug case the International Criminal Court had
investigated Maduro for years.

White House suspends Microsoft from green card program for skilled foreign workers over H-1B visa abuse allegations
Hurricane Isaias could make landfall on northern Gulf Coast late Friday or early Saturday as first Atlantic hurricane of 2026
Aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln returns to San Diego after more than 10 months at sea
Shipping threats increase in Strait of Hormuz due to U.S. war with Iran and in Black Sea due to Russia-Ukraine war
